question: I have only Basic Autoplan and caused a crash in B.C. What coverage distinction matters before I assume my own car's repairs will be paid?
generated_answer:
In B.C., if you only have Basic Autoplan and you cause a crash, the coverage distinction that matters is whether you have collision coverage. Basic Autoplan typically includes third-party liability coverage, which pays for damages to others, but it may not cover damages to your own vehicle unless you have collision coverage.

If you don't have collision coverage, you'll likely be responsible for paying for the repairs to your own vehicle. However, if the other party involved in the crash is at fault, their insurance may cover the damages to your vehicle, but you'll need to work with their insurer to make a claim.

It's important to review your policy documents or contact your insurer to confirm the specifics of your coverage. If you're unsure, it's best to assume that you'll need to pay for the repairs yourself and then seek reimbursement from the other party's insurer if they're found to be at fault.

In any case, it's always a good idea to report the accident to your insurer and follow their instructions for filing a claim. They can guide you through the process and help you understand your coverage and any potential out-of-pocket costs.
